A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SounDiT/GeoS2L and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF includes an appendix, although v1 contains unresolved 'Appendix ??' references.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original generation results on four dataset groups, architectural and retrieval ablations, and a matching user study.

after.justification: Section 6 reports original results on SoundingSVI and SonicUrban, component and expert-count ablations, scene-conditioned examples, and a matching user study.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 substantially redesigns SounDiT. Separate audio/T5 conditioning becomes shared ImageBind conditioning; scene cross-attention is replaced by SLRCM and S-AdaLN. The audio experts gain shared keys/values, low-rank queries and gated top-k aggregation. The geo-contextual retrieval and initialization pipeline described in v1 is removed.

E1.justification: Evaluation on the 6,713-pair geo-contextual VGGSound subset and the 1,889-pair IntoTheWild/Landscape combination disappears. V2 evaluates only the two proposed datasets, substantially narrowing benchmark coverage. The removed benchmarks remain mentioned in the dataset survey, but are no longer evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds PixArt+MHCA to the main comparisons on both retained datasets. CoDi, Sound2Scene, the three AudioToken configurations and GlueGen remain. An MHCA alternative already appeared in v1's SoundingSVI ablation, but was not a comparator in its main results table.

E3.justification: SoundingSVI changes from 334,495 to 169,221 pairs, with newly reported temporal-gap filtering; SonicUrban changes from 250,310 to 236,674 pairs. Scene-classifier annotations are replaced by Qwen2.5-VL-7b prompts. V2 also introduces controlled two-expert component ablations and a 2/4/6/8-expert sweep. These are substantial reported setting changes; comparable reruns of the retained baselines are not documented.

E4.justification: V1's TA-PMoE-versus-MHCA and retrieval-on/off ablations are replaced by individual and joint removal of SLRCM/S-AdaLN and expert-count scaling experiments in v2 Tables 3–4. V2 Figure 4 additionally tests scene control by varying prompts for fixed bird and traffic soundscapes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's disclosure of 17 user-study participants adds sample-size information, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: SounDiT's reported FID changes from 28.173 to 16.839 on SoundingSVI and from 33.246 to 11.553 on SonicUrban; other scores also change. These are revised-model/dataset results, not established same-setting gains. External benchmark results disappear and new component/scaling results appear. The retained original baseline scores and user-study accuracy of 86.13% remain identical.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.3 adds substantive mathematical definitions for scene-dependent low-rank modulation, residual strength, low-rank expert queries and gated top-k aggregation in Equations 5–11. Router prototypes are redefined from expert representations to learnable parameters. The diffusion preliminaries, task objective and PSS definitions remain equivalent; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The Introduction redefines the central model contribution around three explicitly novel components: MoE Soundscape Conditioning, SLRCM and S-AdaLN. The Conclusion now emphasizes a scalable architecture capturing both soundscape and scene context. The broader contributions of GeoS2L, two datasets and PSS remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of soundscape-to-scene ambiguity and expands interpretations concerning urban design, noise mitigation and accessibility. It removes v1's discussion of poor small-benchmark performance and its explicit limitations concerning spatial inaccuracies and restricted PSS coverage. Architectural interpretations shift from retrieval benefits to scene injection and expert scaling.

D1.justification: V2 discloses guidance and initialization values, including training guidance 1.0, alpha initialized to zero and inference CFG 4.0. It adds H100 hardware, the user-study participant count and a project-page link. Conversely, v1's explicit PixArt-alpha initialization statement is no longer provided. These are limited reproducibility-information changes.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes its contextual conditioning from earlier geographic diffusion work, including the newly cited Soundscape-to-Panorama. It adds Qwen, OmniBind and planning/noise/restoration references while dropping T5 and several navigation/ecology references. The broad positioning against generic audio-to-image synthesis remains.

P1.justification: The Abstract and Introduction are extensively rewritten, and the method narrative and metric explanations are substantially reworked. Terminology changes from audio2image to A2I, practical applications receive a dedicated discussion, and limitations are replaced by acknowledgements. The broad seven-section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 switches throughout to a two-column layout and redraws the architecture diagram. It removes the dataset-sample and PSS-framework figures, replaces the qualitative comparison grid, and adds scene-conditioned examples. The dataset table loses two descriptive columns, PSS formulas move from a table into equations, and the results/ablation displays are reorganized.

improvement.justification: V2 improves architectural documentation and adds a closer PixArt+MHCA comparison, targeted component ablations and expert scaling. However, it removes both external benchmark evaluations and explicit limitations. All retained original baseline scores remain unchanged despite revised dataset construction, without documentation establishing comparable evaluation. The stronger architectural evidence and reduced generalization evidence create material tradeoffs whose net effect on paper quality cannot be reliably determined.
